exposure: societal values based on religious beliefs
mobile phone ownership and health information receipt
lack of availability of female doctors
cohort: The study included 943 respondents from urban and rural areas of Bangladesh, comprising 317 pregnant women or women who delivered in the last year, 312 husbands, 262 mothers-in-law, and elderly relatives.
finding: Despite women receiving more maternal health information and having higher educational attainment, husbands and mothers-in-law are the most influential decision-makers regarding maternal health service utilization in Bangladesh, with sociocultural factors and fear of C-section also acting as barriers.
mod_finding: Fear of caesarean section was identified as a primary reason for not utilizing institutional delivery services.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from pregnant women or those who delivered in the last one year.
